headline: The global squeeze died in one session — SMH -8.0% and NVDA back to 152 — but the money rotated into staples, retail and biotech rather than leaving the tape.
summary: Yesterday's melt-up was a gamma event, and it fully round-tripped in semis. NVDA -7.7% to 152.33 after printing 165.05, MU -11.0%, AMD -10.7%, SOXX -8.9%, SMH -8.0%, TSM -6.0%, ASML -4.3%. But the index damage was contained: NDX -2.4%, SPX -0.9%, DJI +0.2%, RUT +0.1%. Underneath, breadth actually improved — RSP/SPY +1.2% to the 91st percentile of its year with a 1m z of 2.23, IWM/SPY +0.9%, QQQ/SPY -1.5% to the 5th percentile. Software held while silicon broke: IGV +0.5%, IGV/SMH +9.2% on the day and +7.8% on the month. This is an AI-capex de-rating with an internal rotation, not an indiscriminate liquidation. SMH's relative strength vs the S&P is now -14.7% over 1m and -18.6% over 3m.

What the squeeze did not fix: volatility, credit, or collateral. VIX +5.9% to 28.18 (+44.9% on the month, z=1.72), VIX3M +4.7% to 26.71, and VIX/VIX3M back up to 1.055 — still backwardated, still rising. Spreads never participated in any rally: HY OAS 3.76 (+49bp 1m), CCC 14.02 (+95bp 1m, +365bp 3m), BBB 1.22, IG 0.98 — all four sitting at the 100th percentile of the past year, with HYG/IEF at a 1m z of -1.22. Crypto printed another lower low: BTC 59,792 (-25.3% 1m, 3rd percentile), ETH -27.8% 1m, SOL -31.7% 1m, MSTR -45.6% 1m, COIN -36.8% 1m. And yesterday's one bullish new development — precious metals bouncing off forced-seller lows — reversed hard: gold -1.8% to 3,586, silver -4.8%, platinum -4.6%, GDXJ -2.8%, with the gold/silver ratio +3.1% to 87.3, the 100th percentile. Collateral is still being sold.

The macro is a disinflation shock colliding with a front end that still hasn't been told. Brent 86.84, -25.6% on the month; gasoline -25.3%; DBC with a 1m z of -3.16 and acceleration -2.54; 5y breakevens 2.15 and 10y 2.13, both the 0th percentile of the year. Yet the 3m bill is 4.32% against an effective funds rate of 3.88%, the 10y real yield is 2.77% at the 85th percentile and 22% above its 200-day, and 30y mortgages are 7.28%. The belly is finally moving — 2y 4.63 (-25bp in a week), 5y 4.71 (-27bp), 10y 4.92 (-23bp) — and that is where the next leg of relief comes from. Natural gas is the only commodity bid: +15.2% today to 3.669, +39.0% on the month, acceleration z=1.91, against crude's collapse.

Own the dispersion. The rotation winners added to their lead today: XLV +2.5% (rel. strength +9.0%/+12.5%), IBB +3.4%, XBI +3.9%, LLY +3.2%, IHI +2.1%; XRT +2.3% with XRT/SPY +8.7% on the month, TGT +4.3% (+15.6% 1m, 100th percentile), WMT +2.0%, MCD +12.5% 1m with z=2.29, HD +9.3% 1m; ITB +1.7%, DHI +2.9%. The cycle still says no: copper -3.1% (-15.8% 1m, z=-2.46), COPX -5.4%, FCX -6.1%, XME -3.5%, CAT -2.5% with a 1m z of -2.49, AUDUSD z=-2.10. The dollar eased marginally — DXY 103.87 (-0.4%), USDBRL -1.5% after a +16.0% month, USDCHF -0.6% — but USDMXN +1.3% to its 100th percentile says the EM funding squeeze isn't over. Risk regime -18, credit & vol -58, inflation composite still 63.

good.text: Breadth improved on a red tape: RSP/SPY +1.2% to the 91st percentile (1m z=2.23), equal-weight S&P only -1.5% on the month vs SPX -5.9%, IWM/SPY +0.9%. The selling is concentrated in AI silicon, not the market.

The disinflation shock is now overwhelming: Brent -25.6% and gasoline -25.3% on the month, DBC with a 1m z of -3.16, 5y breakevens 2.15 and 10y 2.13 at the 0th percentile. The 2y has responded, -25bp in a week to 4.63.
Health care is the cleanest uptrend on the board: XLV +2.5% with relative strength +9.0%/+12.5%, IBB +3.4%, XBI +3.9%, LLY +3.2% (+10.7% 1m), IHI +2.1%.
Consumer cash machines keep compounding: TGT +4.3% (+15.6% 1m, 100th percentile), MCD +12.5% 1m with z=2.29, WMT +10.2% 1m, HD +9.3% 1m, COST +9.1% 1m, XRT/SPY +8.7% on the month.
Housing is quietly turning up on lower mortgage rates: ITB +1.7% (+4.7% 1m), XHB/SPY +8.5% on the month, DHI +2.9%, 30y mortgage -12bp over a month with acceleration z=-1.82, starts +9.9%.
The dollar wall cracked a little: DXY -0.4% to 103.87, USDBRL -1.5% after a +16.0% month, USDCHF -0.6%, USDCNY -0.4%. Not a trend change yet, but the marginal funding pressure eased.

bad.text: The semiconductor squeeze fully reversed in one session: SMH -8.0%, SOXX -8.9%, NVDA -7.7% to 152.33, MU -11.0%, AMD -10.7%, TSM -6.0%. SMH/SPY is -14.7% over a month at the 21st percentile — the AI leadership trade is being de-rated, not just shaken.

Volatility is re-accelerating from an already elevated base: VIX +5.9% to 28.18 (+44.9% 1m, z=1.72), VIX3M +4.7% to 26.71, and the term structure at 1.055 — backwardation deepening, acceleration z=+0.42.
Credit never ratified any of this: HY OAS 3.76 (+49bp 1m), CCC 14.02 (+95bp 1m, +365bp 3m), BBB 1.22, IG 0.98 — all at the 100th percentile of the year, HYG/IEF with a 1m z of -1.22.
Crypto made another low while equities bounced — the clean liquidity tell. BTC 59,792 (-25.3% 1m, 3rd percentile), ETH -27.8%, SOL -31.7%, MSTR -45.6% on the month, COIN -36.8%.
Collateral liquidation resumed in metals, undoing yesterday's bounce: gold -1.8%, silver -4.8%, platinum -4.6%, GDXJ -2.8%, gold/silver +3.1% to 87.3 at the 100th percentile.
Cyclicals and high beta are still making lows: copper -3.1% (1m z=-2.46), COPX -5.4%, FCX -6.1%, XME -3.5%, CAT z=-2.49, SPHB/SPLV -5.8% on the day to the 5th percentile, MTUM 1m z=-2.69.

trades.name: Software over silicon
trades.line: Long IGV / short SMH: the AI capex de-rating has legs
trades.expr: Long IGV, short SMH, dollar-neutral. Size 1:1; roll monthly.
trades.thesis: The AI trade is bifurcating. Hardware is being de-rated on capex-cycle and financing risk (CCC spreads +365bp over 3m fund the hyperscaler buildout tail), while software's cash-flow model is untouched. IGV held green on a day SMH fell 8%.
trades.trigger: IGV +0.5% versus SMH -8.0% today; IGV/SMH +9.2% on the session, +7.8% on the month, turning up. SMH relative strength vs S&P -14.7% 1m, -18.6% 3m; NVDA -7.7% gave back half of a +31.5% squeeze day.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH back below its level before yesterday's squeeze, i.e. the pair giving back 6%; or SMH reclaiming its 200-day (currently -19.3% below it).
trades.target: Another 12% on the ratio, taking IGV/SMH toward the 3m gain of +23.4%.

trades.name: Health care funded by the Nasdaq
trades.line: Long IBB+XBI vs short QQQ: the only clean uptrend left
trades.expr: Long 50% IBB / 50% XBI against a short in QQQ, equal dollars.
trades.thesis: Biotech has the rarest combination on the board right now: positive absolute trend, positive relative trend, falling real yields and zero exposure to the AI capex unwind. QQQ is the funding leg with the worst internals.
trades.trigger: IBB +3.4% and XBI +3.9% today against NDX -2.4%; XLV relative strength +9.0% 1m / +12.5% 3m and up-trending; LLY +3.2%, IHI +2.1%. QQQ/SPY at the 5th percentile of its 52-week range.
trades.stop: Pair down 5%, or XBI losing its 200-day (currently +6.5% above it) while QQQ reclaims its own.
trades.target: +9% on the pair as the health care relative-strength trend extends.

trades.name: Cash flow over beta
trades.line: Long XRT+XLP vs short SPHB as high beta breaks down
trades.expr: Long 50% XRT / 50% XLP, short SPHB, equal dollars.
trades.thesis: A $25 drop in crude is a direct transfer to the US consumer, and the tape is already paying for it. Meanwhile the high-beta cohort is being forcibly deleveraged alongside crypto and semis.
trades.trigger: SPHB/SPLV -5.8% today to the 5th percentile of its year (1m z=-2.09). XRT +2.3% with XRT/SPY +8.7% on the month (z=1.75); XLP relative strength +10.8%/+14.3%; TGT +4.3%, WMT +2.0%, MCD +12.5% 1m. Gasoline -25.3% on the month.
trades.stop: Pair down 5%, or SPHB/SPLV recovering above its 200-day (currently -16.3% below).
trades.target: +8% on the pair; exit if HY OAS compresses back under 3.25.

trades.name: Gas over oil
trades.line: Long natgas / short Brent: the only commodity with a bid
trades.expr: Long front natural gas futures against short Brent, equal notional; roll before expiry.
trades.thesis: The energy complex has split. Crude is in a supply-driven collapse dragging breakevens to the 0th percentile; natural gas is a domestic, weather- and power-demand asset that is breaking higher independent of the global growth scare.
trades.trigger: Natgas +15.2% today to 3.669, +39.0% on the month with acceleration z=+1.91 and turning up; Brent -2.8% to 86.84, -25.6% on the month, 1m z=-2.57 and acceleration -2.54. XOP -18.0% and OIH -16.0% on the month confirm the crude side.
trades.stop: Natgas back under 3.20, or Brent reclaiming 92 on an OPEC/geopolitical supply headline.

trades.name: Crypto equity beta
trades.line: Short MSTR and COIN: new BTC low, no squeeze participation
trades.expr: Short an equal-weight basket of MSTR and COIN; or buy 2-month put spreads on each.
trades.thesis: Crypto equities are levered claims on a bid that no longer exists. Equities squeezed 5-7% yesterday and bitcoin still made a lower low — that is a funding signature. MSTR's collateral model does not survive a sustained sub-60k bitcoin.
trades.trigger: BTC 59,792, -2.3% today and -25.3% on the month, 3rd percentile of its year; IBIT -26.4% 1m; MSTR -6.0% today, -17.8% in a week, -45.6% on the month; COIN -4.5% to 103.86 at the 1st percentile. SOL -31.7% 1m.
trades.stop: Bitcoin back above 68,000, or a 15% adverse move in the basket on a leverage-driven short squeeze.
trades.target: +20% on the short basket toward a BTC retest of 52-54k.

trades.name: Own the belly
trades.line: Long IEF: passive tightening meets a 0th-percentile breakeven
trades.expr: Long IEF outright (7-10y Treasuries); add on any back-up above 4.95% in the 10y.
trades.thesis: Real policy is tightening while nominal growth collapses. The 10y real yield at 2.77% sits at the 85th percentile and 22% above its 200-day, the 3m bill at 4.32% is 44bp above effective funds, and 5y breakevens at 2.15 are the lowest of the year. Something has to give, and it is the belly of the curve.
trades.trigger: 5y -27bp and 10y -23bp over the week; 10y real -11bp; T5YIE -33bp on the month (z=-1.58) and T10YIE -21bp, both the 0th percentile; 3m10y flattened 23bp in a week to 55bp; DBC 1m z=-3.16.
trades.stop: 10y back above 5.15%, or core CPI accelerating further from +30bp m/m with the inflation composite above 63.

trades.name: India over Taiwan
trades.line: Long INDA / short EWT: cheap oil beats the chip cycle
trades.expr: Long INDA against short EWT, equal dollars.
trades.thesis: A $25 crude collapse is the single biggest terms-of-trade gift to India, and the rupee is confirming it. Taiwan is pure semiconductor beta into a de-rating, and yesterday's +9% catch-up gap is prime supply.
trades.trigger: INDA +12.8% on the month with a 1m z of 2.87 and acceleration +2.54, relative strength +19.8%/+11.4%; USDINR -1.9% on the month. EWT -5.1% today and -20.2% on the month; TWII rel. strength -7.0%/-5.2%; TSM -6.0%.
trades.stop: Pair down 6%, or INDA's 1m momentum z falling back below 1 while semis reclaim their 200-day.
